nutshell: Today's items point to AI moving into everyday tooling: coding agents are spreading into games, video, gadgets and apps, with MCP and Claude Code appearing across many projects. Small, efficient local models such as Inkling-2-Mini keep getting easier to run on modest hardware. At the same time, security and governance concerns are rising, from leaked secrets in agent tooling to hosted agent sandboxes and data-processing incidents at inference providers.

items.title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets Through Its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
items.snippet: Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos. By Sergio De Simone
